We verified the R log-domain Sinkhorn implementation against the Python POT library on the full skill-cost matrix. Both solutions satisfied marginal constraints to <1e−11 and agreed to numerical precision (max absolute difference 2.8e−12; relative Frobenius difference 3.5e−10).

The entropy-regularized transport model is equivalent to a doubly-constrained gravity model of occupational mobility, where distance is defined either by skill similarity or by institutional hierarchy.

By conditioning on the observed marginals, the transport model eliminates the main identification problem in gravity models: separating distance effects from origin/destination size effects.

Modern gravity estimation includes origin and destination fixed effects:

These absorb size differences.

But two issues remain:

1️⃣ Marginals are only matched in expectation

The estimated flows generally do not exactly match observed totals.

2️⃣ Identification can still be weak

Because:

fixed effects soak up huge variation

distance effects can become sensitive to specification.

Because the transport model conditions on observed origin and destination totals, occupational growth and decline are imposed by the data. The model is therefore evaluated solely on its ability to rationalize bilateral substitution patterns across occupations.


SafeSink prioritizes correctness over raw speed by enforcing name-based alignment and numerical stability.
Log-domain Sinkhorn (numerically stable)
Dimension-safe inputs (no silent alignment bugs)
Built-in validation tools


# Core Question

## What distance metric is better at rationalizing occupational mobility?

- When workers change occupations, are frictions governed by:

  - Smooth similarity in skills and abilities?
  - Discrete institutional and credential boundaries?

- Conditioning on observed marginals separates:

  - Extensive margin of reallocation (how many move)
  - Composition of reallocation (who moves to where)

- Distance is the not the only determinant of mobility — but conditional on net reallocation volumes, distance should structure where flows come from if either distance metric represents an economically meaningful friction.
